parameters.content: Receives the incoming request from Bidsquire when an admin submits a HiBid URL. Payload contains url_main, itemId, adminId, and adminEmail.
Calls the HiBid scraper service to extract the listing data. Returns title, lot number, images array, and URL
Combines the scraper output with the webhook payload into one clean object. Also derives a category from title keywords and strips lot number prefixes from the title.
Searches the item_db library for existing items that match this category or title. Used to check if we've seen something similar before.
Cleans the title further for searching — strips noise words, lot prefixes, and special characters. Also runs a heuristic check for fake risk keywords and non-exact-matchable item types.
Sends the cleaned search query to Serper (Google Search API) to find real-world listings, sold prices, and product references for this item.
Extracts the organic results and peopleAlsoAsk sections from the Serper response and formats them into clean text for Claude to read.
Claude reads the search results and decides: is this an exact matchable item, what is the confidence score, is there a fake risk, and what brand or maker's marks are present.
Parses Claude's JSON response and determines the match type — exact (≥0.9 confidence), category (≥0.5), or none. Carries all match data forward.
Creates a new row in the item_db library for this item type, or increments times_seen if a similar item already exists. This is how the library grows organically.
Creates a match record linking this specific Bidsquire auction item to its item_db row. All appraiser and critic results will be written to this record.
Captures the item_db item ID and match ID from the previous two nodes and carries them forward so all downstream nodes can reference them.
Strips thumbnail size parameters from HiBid image URLs to get full resolution versions. Generates the R2 key and public URL for each image before upload.
Downloads each image binary from the HiBid CDN so it can be re-uploaded to our own storage.
Uploads the downloaded image to Cloudflare R2 under the item-db/ prefix. Images are stored here permanently for matching and analysis.
Records the R2 URL and source URL in the item_db_images table so we know exactly where each image lives and where it came from.
Fetches the stored R2 URLs for this item from the database so Claude can analyze them. Uses R2 URLs instead of HiBid CDN URLs because HiBid blocks external access
Formats the R2 image URLs into a comma-separated string ready to pass into Claude's image analysis node.
Constructs the Basic Auth header using the eBay API credentials for the OAuth token request.
Exchanges the eBay credentials for a short-lived OAuth access token using the client_credentials grant. Required for all eBay API calls.
Searches eBay's Browse API for active and recently sold listings matching this item. Returns up to 20 results with prices and conditions.
Strips outlier prices that fall outside the main cluster (the "seller didn't know what they had" problem). Computes trimmed min, max, and median. Selects the 6 best reference URLs.
Writes the raw prices, trimmed prices, removed outliers, and reference URLs to the item_db price history table. Full audit trail for every market data pull.
Claude vision analyzes up to 4 images of the item. Describes condition, visible damage, makers marks, material, and age indicators. This feeds directly into the appraisal prompt.
Combines Claude's image analysis text with the price range data so the appraiser has everything it needs in one object.
Claude acts as a professional auction appraiser. Using the item details, market range, and image analysis it produces a price estimate, eBay listing description, and fake risk assessment.
Parses Claude's JSON response from attempt 1. Falls back to safe defaults if the response can't be parsed.
Writes the attempt 1 appraisal result to the item_db match record for audit and comparison purposes.

A separate Claude instance acts as a senior auction expert and evaluates the appraisal. Checks if the estimate is within the market range, if the description is specific, and if fake risk is communicated properly.
Parses the critic's JSON response. Extracts passed/failed, score, failure reason, and suggestions for the retry.
Writes the critic round 1 result to the item_db match record including the failure reason that will be injected into attempt 2.
Routes the workflow — if the critic passed, goes straight to finalization. If failed, sends to appraiser attempt 2 with the critic's feedback.
Packages the attempt 1 appraisal as the final result when critic round 1 passes.
Claude tries again with the critic's specific failure reason injected into the prompt. Knows exactly what was wrong and what to fix.
Parses Claude's JSON response from attempt 2.
Writes the attempt 2 appraisal result to the item_db match record.
Final evaluation. Same criteria as round 1 but slightly more lenient if genuine improvements were made. If this fails, the item goes to human review.
Parses the critic round 2 response.
Writes the critic round 2 result to the item_db match record.
Final routing decision — passes to finalization or flags for human review.
Packages the attempt 2 appraisal as the final result when critic round 2 passes.
Consolidates the winning appraisal (attempt 1 or 2), priority level, and reference URLs into one clean object for the final callback.
Writes the final approved estimate, description, and reference URLs to the item_db match record. Status set to critic_passed.
Posts the complete result back to Bidsquire — item data, AI estimate, description, and match confidence. Updates the placeholder item to research status so it appears in the researcher dashboard.
Only fires if both critic rounds fail. Sets the item_db match status to human_review so the team can manually review and tune the critic thresholds during testing.
